accountSettingsYouTubeCookieForm: Import from a browser. Sign in with the session of a browser you signed in to YouTube Music with. Browser. Profile. Another profile than the browser's own, by its name or its folder. MixMusic finds those of Zen, Helium and the browsers installed as Flatpaks in their folders. Import. MixMusic reads the browser's cookies with yt-dlp, keeps YouTube's alone, encrypted on this computer, and deletes the rest at once. Close the browser first: while it's open, it may hold its cookies, or not have saved a new sign-in yet. Recent Chrome on Windows seals its cookies against other programs: use Firefox there, or paste a cookie header. Paste a cookie header. In a tab signed in to music.youtube.com, open the developer tools, and copy the Cookie header of a request to music.youtube.com from the Network panel. The text of a cookies.txt file will do too. Sign in with it. Log in. A cookie header is as good as your password: paste it here alone. YouTube may end a session that goes on in the browser; one from a private window you then close lasts longest.

Tracks play as they do signed out, unless Play audio as your account is on: then yt-dlp asks as your account first. copiesFindLabel: Find a song of this computer
copiesFindPlaceholder: find a song of this computer
copiesNoMatch: No other song of this computer matches that.

@crossfadeGaplessDesc.description: In Settings › Playback › Sound, under Keep albums gapless (crossfadeGapless): what the switch does. 'The step out of an album' is the change from an album's last song played to a track of something else.

desktopSettingsAutostartReason: MixMusic starts when you log in, as you chose in its settings

@desktopSettingsAutostartReason.description: Why MixMusic asks to start at login, which the Linux desktop shows as it asks the user.

@desktopSettingsAutostartRefused.description: Why Start at login (desktopSettingsLogin) didn't turn on, as a toast.

desktopSettingsAutostartStays: the desktop still starts MixMusic at login

@desktopSettingsAutostartStays.description: Why Start at login (desktopSettingsLogin) didn't turn off, as a toast.

desktopSettingsBackgroundReason: MixMusic plays on in the tray when you close its window

@desktopSettingsBackgroundReason.description: Why MixMusic asks to run in the background, which the Linux desktop shows as it asks the user.

desktopSettingsDiscordAbout: While Discord runs, your profile says what you listen to: you choose its lines, cover, time and button.
desktopSettingsDiscordAppIDAbout: Discord shows the name of MixMusic's application. To show another, create one in the {link} and paste its application ID.

@desktopSettingsDiscordAppIDAbout.description: Under Settings › Desktop › Discord's application ID. {link} is desktopSettingsDiscordPortal, a link to Discord's page.

desktopSettingsMediaKeysAbout: The keyboard's play, next and previous keys control MixMusic. Keys of your own that work everywhere are in Settings › Shortcuts.
desktopSettingsNoBackgroundPortal: this desktop has no Background portal, which a Flatpak app needs to start at login: add MixMusic to the apps your desktop starts at login instead

@desktopSettingsNoBackgroundPortal.description: Why Start at login (desktopSettingsLogin) didn't turn on, as a toast, for MixMusic installed from Flathub. The Background portal is a part of Linux desktops.

desktopSettingsNoJsonApp: no app on this computer opens .json files, so MixMusic showed settings.json in its folder

@desktopSettingsNoJsonApp.description: Toast after Open settings.json, in Settings › Desktop, when no app opens .json files. settings.json is the file's name.

desktopSettingsNotificationsAbout: Tell what starts playing while MixMusic is in the background.
desktopSettingsResetAbout: Puts back the settings of a new install; your accounts, library and add-ons stay.
desktopSettingsResetConfirm: Put back every setting as it was on a new install?
desktopSettingsSettingsFileAbout: Your settings, as settings.json in your data folder. Save it while MixMusic runs, and they apply at once.
desktopSettingsTitleAbout: The window's title names the track that plays, for the taskbar, the window switcher and screen readers.
desktopSettingsTitleTitle: Show what plays in the window title
desktopSettingsTrayAbout: Closing the window keeps the music playing; quit from the tray icon.

@discordBadgeFile.description: What the small mark on the cover of the Discord status says as it is hovered, for a file on the listener's computer. Others read it on the listener's profile.

@discordBadgePaused.description: What the small mark on the cover of the Discord status says as it is hovered, while the track is paused.

discordCoverDescription: Discord shows the cover of what plays, where its service has one online: a file on your computer shows none.
discordKeepWhilePausedDescription: A paused track stays, marked as paused, without its time. Off, pausing clears the status.
discordKeepWhilePausedLabel: Keep the Discord status while paused
discordListenButtonDescription: A button that opens the track on YouTube Music or Spotify, which the others who see your profile can click. A file on your computer has none.
discordListenButtonLabel: Show a Listen button on Discord

@discordListenOn.description: The button of the Discord status that opens the track on its service, which others click on the listener's profile. Discord cuts it after 32 characters.

@discordMyComputer.description: The service of a file on the listener's computer, as {service} of a line of the Discord status says it, as in "on my computer". Others read it on the listener's profile.

discordNothingPlays: Nothing plays: this is how a song would show.
discordPlaceholdersLabel: Placeholders: {placeholders}. Empty, the line shows nothing.

@discordPlaceholdersLabel.description: Under a line of the Discord status. {placeholders} lists the placeholders the line may hold, as they are typed.

discordPreviewPausedNote: While paused, your profile shows nothing: this shows once the track plays again.
discordServiceBadgeDescription: A small mark of YouTube Music, Spotify or a file on your computer, at the cover's corner, or in its place.
discordServiceBadgeLabel: Show the service's badge on Discord
discordTimeLeftDescription: How long the track has played, and how long it has left.
discordTimeLeftLabel: Show the time left on Discord
discordUnknownNote: {count, plural, one {{names} isn't a placeholder, and shows as typed.} other {{names} aren't placeholders, and show as typed.}}

@dislikeNoteSee.description: Under Skip songs you dislike, once there are some. {link} is dislikeSee, a link to the list of them.

@downloadsCancelOne.description: Tooltip and label of the button that cancels one download.

downloadsCollectionPartial: Downloading {title}: the {kept} of its {total} tracks MixMusic reads
downloadsConfirmMessage: That's about {size}. They play without the network, and stay until you remove them.

@downloadsConfirmTitle.description: Title of the question before a big download.

downloadsHoldMetered: Waiting for a connection that isn't metered, as set in Settings › Playback

@downloadsHoldOffline.description: Why the downloads wait, on the downloads page.

@downloadsHoldPaused.description: Why the downloads wait, on the downloads page: the user paused them.

downloadsHoldThrottled: YouTube is turning down requests from this network for now; downloads go on in a while

@downloadsHoldThrottled.description: Why the downloads wait, on the downloads page.

@downloadsMenuShowTracks.description: Menu item of a downloaded album, playlist or mix.

@downloadsMove.description: Confirm button of moving the downloads. Lowercase.

@downloadsReasonExplicit.description: Why a track couldn't download: it is explicit, or, of a Spotify track, its recording on YouTube Music that downloads in its place is, and Hide explicit content in Settings › Playback is on. It goes in the {reason} of downloadsMarkFailed and downloadsStatusFailed, so it starts in lowercase where the language has cases.

downloadsReasonNeedsYTDLP: it needs yt-dlp, which Settings › Playback installs

@downloadsStatusWaiting.description: Status of a track in the queue. Lowercase.

@downloadsStop.description: Confirm button of cancelling every download. Lowercase.

firewallAllowed: Windows Firewall lets MixMusic in on private networks

firewallBlocked: Windows Firewall keeps other computers and cast devices on this network from reaching MixMusic, as it does once its question about MixMusic is answered with Cancel. Allow lets them in on private networks, with an administrator's approval.
firewallDefault: Windows Firewall keeps other computers and cast devices on this network from reaching MixMusic, and doesn't ask about apps. Allow lets them in on private networks, with an administrator's approval.
firewallLetsIn: Windows Firewall lets other computers and cast devices on this network reach MixMusic, for remote control and casting.

firewallOff: Windows Firewall is off for this network, so other computers and cast devices on it reach MixMusic, for remote control and casting.
firewallPublic: Windows counts this network as public, so Windows Firewall keeps other computers and cast devices on it from reaching MixMusic. If you trust the network, as the one at home, make it private in Windows' network settings.
firewallReading: Reading whether Windows Firewall lets other computers and cast devices on this network reach MixMusic…
firewallShielded: Windows Firewall blocks every incoming connection on this network, those of the apps it allows too, so other computers and cast devices can't reach MixMusic. Windows Security turns that off, in Firewall & network protection.

loudnessEvenDesc: Turns loud tracks down to one level, from YouTube's measure of each, so none jumps out. Quiet recordings keep their level.
loudnessEvenDescSpotify: Turns loud tracks down to one level, from YouTube's measure of each, so none jumps out. Quiet recordings keep their level. Spotify plays its own tracks at its own loudness.
loudnessLevellingDesc: Squeezes loud and quiet moments closer together as they play, and lifts quiet recordings.
lyricBallBoomerangAbout: Thrown out past the end of the line, it curves back to the next.
lyricBallDiveAbout: It rises a little, as to gather itself, and drops to the next line.
lyricBallHopAbout: One arc, as the hops between words are.
lyricBallLoopAbout: A loop over the last word, then a swoop to the next line.
lyricBallMixAbout: A different motion for each line, in turn.
lyricBallRicochetAbout: It bounces off the right edge of the lyrics and their floor.
lyricStyleSettingsBallDesc: A ball hops from word to word over the line sung, as its words are sung, and flies to the next line. Only for lyrics timed word by word.
lyricStyleSettingsPreviewDesc: how the full-screen lyrics look in the style, size and ball set
lyricStyleSettingsStageDesc: Cover the window with the lyrics of what plays, over its blurred cover.
lyricsCantLoad: Lyrics can't be loaded right now. Check your connection, or try again in a moment.

@lyricsCantLoad.description: In the lyrics' place, where the sources can't be reached.

lyricsCaptionLanguageDescription: Lyrics from YouTube captions come in this language when the video has captions in it, and in the video's own else.

@lyricsCreditFrom.description: Under the lyrics: where they come from. {source} is the name of the lyrics' source, a link to it where its licence asks for one.

@lyricsCreditFromBy.description: Under the lyrics: where they come from, and who gave them to it. {source} is the name of the source and {by} the name of the person, each a link to its page where the source asks for one.

lyricsEditAbout: Correct a word or a line. A time in brackets, as [01:02.50], is when the line after it is sung, and one in angle brackets, as <01:02.50>, when the word after it is. Your edit shows for this track until you pick another source or Automatic.

@lyricsEditAbout.description: At the top of lyricsEditTitle. Keep the times as they are written: [01:02.50] and <01:02.50>. "Automatic" is lyricsSourceAutomatic.

lyricsEditEmpty: These lyrics have no words to keep.

@lyricsEditEmpty.description: In lyricsEditTitle, under the text box, when the listener saves it with no words in it.

@lyricsEditLabel.description: For screen readers: the text box of lyricsEditTitle, which holds the lyrics to correct.

@lyricsEditTitle.description: The title of the dialog lyricsSourceEdit opens: the lyrics shown, as text to correct.

lyricsKanjiDownloading: The readings of kanji are downloading: kanji show as they are until then.
lyricsKanjiUnavailable: The readings of kanji couldn't be downloaded: kanji show as they are.
lyricsLocalTip: Shows the lyrics in Latin letters too, made on this computer: nothing is sent.
lyricsNotFound: No lyrics found for this track.

@lyricsNotFound.description: In the lyrics' place, where no source has lyrics of the track.

lyricsPlayToSee: Play a track to see its lyrics.
lyricsPreferWordsDescription: Lyrics timed word by word from a source lower in the list show in place of lyrics timed line by line from one above it. It sends the track to more sources.
lyricsRomajiTip: Shows the lyrics in romaji too, made on this computer: nothing is sent. The first time, it downloads the dictionary of the readings of kanji, 11.7 MB, from GitHub.
lyricsRomanizeTip: Shows the lyrics in Latin letters too. While it's on, the lyrics of the track playing and its video ID go to Unison, which has Google romanize them.
lyricsSearchAbout: Every lyrics source that is on gets this title and artist. YouTube Music and YouTube captions look up the track that plays instead.

@lyricsSearchAbout.description: At the top of lyricsSearchTitle: what the sources are sent. YouTube Music and YouTube captions are names.

@lyricsSearchArtist.description: In lyricsSearchTitle: the label of the field of the artist to search for.

@lyricsSearchGo.description: In lyricsSearchTitle: the button that asks the sources for the title and artist in the fields. Lowercase, as the labels of buttons are.

@lyricsSearchLooking.description: In lyricsSearchTitle, while the sources are asked for the title and artist.

@lyricsSearchSongTitle.description: In lyricsSearchTitle: the label of the field of the song's title to search for.

lyricsSearchTitle: Search lyrics by title and artist

@lyricsSearchTitle.description: The title of the dialog lyricsSourceSearch opens: a title and an artist to change, and what each lyrics source found for them.

@lyricsSearchUse.description: In lyricsSearchTitle, the button on a result: shows these lyrics for the track that plays, and keeps the source, title and artist for it. Lowercase, as the labels of buttons are.

@lyricsSearchUseFrom.description: For screen readers: the lyricsSearchUse button on a result of lyricsSearchTitle. {source} is the source's name.

lyricsSettingsDesc: The translate switch beside the lyrics shows them in this language. While it's on, the lyrics of the track playing and its video ID go to Unison, which has Google translate them; nothing is sent while it's off. Lyrics in other scripts show in Latin letters made on this computer, which sends nothing: Japanese in romaji, and the others by the standard of their language. Only Arabic's go to Unison, which romanizes them with the vowels Arabic doesn't write.
lyricsShareChosen: {count, plural, one {# line chosen.} other {# lines chosen.}}

Lowercase, as the other labels there.

lyricsSourceBetterLyricsSent: Lyrics timed word by word. Gets the title, first artist, album and length of tracks that have an album.

lyricsSourceCaptionsSent: The captions of the video that plays, never those made from speech. Gets the video ID, signed out.

@lyricsSourceEdited.description: In the menu of the lyrics sources, and on its button: the lyrics the listener edited with lyricsSourceEdit, which show for the track until another choice replaces them.

@lyricsSourceInstrumental.description: Under a source in the menu of the lyrics sources, and under a result of lyricsSearchTitle: the source has the track as an instrumental, without words.

lyricsSourceLRCLIBSent: Gets the title, artists, album and length; for a music video, its song's.

lyricsSourceUnisonSent: Gets the video ID, or the title, artists, album and length.

@lyricsSourceUnreachable.description: Under a source in the menu of the lyrics sources, and under a result of lyricsSearchTitle: the source couldn't be reached, or answered with an error. Picking it asks it again.

lyricsSourceYouTubeMusicSent: Gets the video ID of the track, or of its recording there.
lyricsSourcesAbout: MixMusic asks the sources that are on, one at a time, from the top, until one has synced lyrics. Drag a source onto another to move it there, or press Alt+Up or Alt+Down on it.
lyricsStyleBoldAbout: Big, heavy, tight letters, like a poster.
lyricsStyleCalmAbout: Small, quiet letters, with a light fade and almost no blur, for a relaxed mood.
lyricsStyleFocusAbout: Bold, even letters. The farther a line is from the one sung, the more it fades and blurs.
lyricsStyleGlowAbout: Round, bold letters with a soft glow on the words as they are sung. The other lines blur.
lyricsStyleSimpleAbout: Plain letters, as in the rest of MixMusic. No blur: the other lines only fade.
lyricsStyleSpotlightAbout: Very big letters. Only the line sung is sharp: the others blur.

lyricsTimeVideosNoteTimedSlower: Timed to this video ({shift} s, {percent}% slower)
lyricsTimeVideosNoteTiming: Timing these lyrics to the video…
lyricsTranslateTip: Shows each line's translation under it. While it's on, the lyrics of the track playing and its video ID go to Unison, which has Google translate them.

lyricsVideoNotSynced: Not synced: the song's synced lyrics don't match this video.

youtubeBrowserForm: MixMusic opens the browser with a new, empty profile of its own, at YouTube Music's sign-in. Sign in there as in any browser: MixMusic then takes the session, closes the browser and deletes the profile. Your own profiles stay as they are. MixMusic signs in through Firefox or Zen, and found neither. Google refuses a sign-in in Chrome, Edge and the others made from Chromium when MixMusic opens them. Closing the browser, or cancel, ends the sign-in, as do 10 minutes without one. MixMusic reads the new profile alone, never yours, and keeps the session encrypted on this computer. Sign in with. Log in. Temporary profile. Google refuses.
